=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
File: scripts/render_prompt.sh
Line or code reference: Lines 46-66 (bash case/esac loop)
Problem: The bash loop replacement only resolves three hardcoded whole-line placeholders (WORKFLOW_EDIT_RESTRICTION, SEMBLE_PREFETCH, SERENA_TOOL_HINTS). The conflict-resolver continuation path at review_conflict_resolve.sh:116-124 sets env vars PREVIOUS_ATTEMPT_NUMBER, MAX_ATTEMPTS, PREVIOUS_ATTEMPT_FAILURE_KIND, MARKER_VIOLATION_COUNT, MARKER_VIOLATION_FILES, FINGERPRINT_VIOLATION_COUNT, FINGERPRINT_VIOLATION_DETAILS and calls render_prompt.sh with continuation templates that contain those as {{PLACEHOLDER}} references. The old delegation to render_prompt.py dynamically resolved any {{VAR}} found in the prompt file by looking up matching shell env vars. The bash loop does not.
Why it fails at runtime: The rendered continuation prompt delivered to Codex will contain literal unresolved strings like {{PREVIOUS_ATTEMPT_NUMBER}} instead of the actual attempt count, producing a nonsensical prompt for the conflict-resolver retry loop.
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

File: scripts/memory_helpers.sh
Line or code reference: Lines 434-436 (deletion of _memory_force_tick_* helper functions including memory_force_tick_get and memory_force_tick_put)
Problem: The deletion removes the shell function definitions for memory_force_tick_get() and memory_force_tick_put().
Why it fails at runtime: tests/test_orchestrate_force_tick.py:test_memory_helpers_export_force_tick_wrappers (lines 467-472) reads scripts/memory_helpers.sh and asserts the literal strings "memory_force_tick_get()" and "memory_force_tick_put()" appear in the file text. After the deletion both assertions will fail. The runtime path in scripts/orchestrate_force_tick.sh uses declare -F guards (lines 335, 371, 393, 433) and fails open so no shell crash occurs, but the test suite breaks.
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

File: scripts/memory_helpers.sh
Line or code reference: lines 434-850 (entire function block deleted)
Problem: The PR deletes `_memory_force_tick_remote_url`, `_memory_force_tick_remote_branch_exists`, `_memory_force_tick_ensure_branch`, `_memory_force_tick_collision_wrapper`, `memory_force_tick_get`, and `memory_force_tick_put` functions.
Why it fails at runtime: `scripts/orchestrate_force_tick.sh` explicitly checks for `memory_force_tick_get` and `memory_force_tick_put` with `declare -F` and calls them. The deletion will cause command-not-found errors and test failures.
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

File: scripts/render_prompt.sh
Line or code reference: lines 43-81 (the case/esac loop)
Problem: Replacing the Python-based prompt rendering delegation with a limited bash loop only resolves three specific placeholders (`{{WORKFLOW_EDIT_RESTRICTION}}`, `{{SEMBLE_PREFETCH}}`, `{{SERENA_TOOL_HINTS}}`) as whole-line matches. The old code dynamically discovered all `{{VAR}}` patterns, enforced prompt contracts from `prompts/contracts/`, applied workflow overlays, and resolved environment-variable-driven placeholders.
Why it fails at runtime: Continuation prompt templates used by `scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh` contain `{{PREVIOUS_ATTEMPT_NUMBER}}`, `{{MAX_ATTEMPTS}}`, `{{PREVIOUS_ATTEMPT_FAILURE_KIND}}`, `{{MARKER_VIOLATION_COUNT}}`, `{{FINGERPRINT_VIOLATION_COUNT}}`, and other placeholders that will remain unresolved, causing malformed prompts to reach the LLM.
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

File: scripts/memory_helpers.sh
Line or code reference: lines 434-850 (functions deleted)
Problem: The deletion removes public shell functions that are called by `scripts/orchestrate_force_tick.sh` and tested by `tests/test_orchestrate_force_tick.py`.
Why it fails at runtime: This is a breaking change to the documented contract - callers expect these functions to exist. No deprecation path or alias was provided.
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

File: scripts/render_prompt.sh
Line or code reference: lines 1-100 (complete rewrite)
Problem: The script's contract was to delegate to `render_prompt.py` for arbitrary placeholder resolution. The rewrite breaks this contract by only handling three hardcoded placeholders.
Why it fails at runtime: Callers that depend on contract validation, workflow overlays, or arbitrary placeholder resolution will now get incomplete or broken output.
